chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
Regarding a man who sells fresh grape juice, and the ruler detains it until it becomes wine, so the owner makes it vinegar; he said: 'When it changes from the name of wine, there is no harm in it.'
ai.seo_question: Is vinegar made from wine that was detained by the government permissible in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'tabdil al-ism' (change of name) as a criterion for permissibility, illustrating how a substance's legal status shifts with its physical transformation. In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the distinction between the inherent impurity of wine and the conditional nature of its prohibition, allowing vinegar derived from it to be consumed once the intoxicating essence is replaced by acidity. This ruling underscores the practical flexibility in dealing with natural processes affecting halal substances.
